chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever strives to fulfill the need of his Muslim brother, seeking the Face of Allah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him a thousand thousand (million) good deeds, and in them He will forgive his relatives, his neighbors, his brothers, his acquaintances, and whoever did him a favor in the world.

So when it is the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to him: 'Enter the Fire.' So whoever you find in it who did you a favor in the world, remove him by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, unless he is a Nasibi (one of the hostile ones).

key_terms.سَعَى فِي حَاجَةِ: striving to fulfill the need of
key_terms.نَاصِباً: Nasibi (hostile one, specifically to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for helping a Muslim brother according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the social dimension of faith, where interceding for a believer’s needs is an act of worship that secures divine forgiveness for one’s entire social network. The unique eschatological mechanism described—where the benefactor is initially directed to Hell but is saved by the very people they helped—illustrates the concept of 'intercession through merit' (Shafa'ah bi'l-Fi'l), a key theme in Shia theology. This highlights how worldly kindness creates a chain of salvation, contingent upon the individual not being a 'Nasibi' (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt).
